page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with two threads per core, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache. Memory provisioning totals 128 GB of RAM, adhering to a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory distribution of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle local storage, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistence, and it is provisioned with a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward parallel throughput rather than single-threaded speed. The processor architecture registers modest single-core metrics, scoring 945.0 on Geekbench single-core and 1108.19 on stress-ng single-core tests. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads leverage the 32 vCPUs effectively, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 23181.17 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8272.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 1308.86 GB/s for small cached reads and maintains 98.48 GB/s for large uncached reads, supporting steady multi-core execution across memory-intensive tasks.

From an efficiency perspective, the instance provides cost-effective compute and memory density for horizontally scaled infrastructure where single-thread latency is not a critical constraint. Its balanced resource profile delivers capable throughput for services like Redis, which records 22.12 million SET operations per second, alongside steady static web serving at 13.89 GB/s. Common deployment targets include distributed web application tiers, mid-tier relational or in-memory databases, batch processing, and CI/CD compilation workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors running at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores alongside 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. It operates without bundled local disk storage, requiring external block storage for persistent data, and provides a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest single-thread execution speeds alongside stable multi-core throughput, demonstrated by balanced scores in PassMark CPU tests and multi-threaded decompression. The instance demonstrates solid handling of concurrent tasks, sustaining 22.12 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.89 GB/s in static web throughput. Without integrated GPUs, the instance is structurally configured for horizontally scaled enterprise backends, in-memory caching tiers, intermediate database processing, and multi-threaded compilation pipelines where high core counts and dependable multi-core density take precedence over peak per-core speed.
